key_insight: A generalizable, systematic prompt-evaluation framework reveals which prompt design features produce more personalized and pedagogically aligned LLM follow-up questions in structured learning dialogues.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of evidence-based methods for designing and evaluating prompts for educational LLM applications, reducing unpredictable or misaligned outputs and enabling reproducible, pedagogically grounded prompt selection.
method: Design and compare multiple prompt templates (six variants) targeting follow-up question generation in a structured dialogue activity.
Evaluate outputs using a mix of automated metrics and human annotation focused on personalization, pedagogical alignment, and quality.
Iteratively analyze template features to identify which constraints and cues improve educational relevance and consistency.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and edtech builders a reproducible way to choose and refine prompts that reliably produce educationally useful, personalized content—reducing trial-and-error and improving classroom suitability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: prompt templates → LLM → automated metrics + human annotation → comparative analysis
Bar chart or radar plot comparing template performance on key metrics (personalization, alignment, coherence, relevance)
Annotated example dialogue pairs (input student turn vs. LLM follow-up) illustrating low- and high-quality prompts
Feature map highlighting prompt components (e.g., pedagogical constraints, personalization cues) and their observed effects
paper_title: LLM Prompt Evaluation for Educational Applications
paper_authors: Langdon Holmes, Adam Coscia, Scott Crossley, Joon Suh Choi, Wesley Morris
